details: CONFIRMED by a probe in a temp repo with the live why copied in: "NESTED accepted". Measured over the live queue with the
branch's quoted_spans: 4 fields have Cyrillic outside every span; 3 of them are the owner's words inside nested double quotes
(the 4th, option-letters-have-no-fixed-alphabet, is the front's own text). The design (section 4 A and section 5) promised:
"The 4 lines whose Russian lies partly outside double quotes (nested quotes) are covered by the joined-span rule or refused as
unbalanced; the build checks each of the 4 by a test" and "an edit of its Russian words is refused". Neither holds: the
quotes balance, so the field is not refused, and the inner word is unprotected. This breaks the owner decision of 26 Oct
(the owner's words are kept verbatim) and the brief's "leaves every quoted span byte-equal": HIGH. Size: 30.
evidence: pytest -q -s scratchpad/qe/test_probe.py -k nested  ->  NESTED accepted: ... (edit of "на глаз" landed)
live scan: fields 1087 unbalanced 0; cyrillic outside spans 4:
queue-time-estimates-are-guesses-with-no-model-b why: '... за этой оценкой, "на глаз" или здесь существует система оценки"'
spans: ['"На сколько оценочное время совпадает с реальным в...', '" или здесь существует система оценки"']
relay-as-a-portable-tool-project-data-out-of-rel why: ... каким может стать "вкус", память это заметки ...
failing_case: Live item queue-time-estimates-are-guesses-with-no-model-b, field why, holds the owner's words
"... что стоит за этой оценкой, "на глаз" или здесь существует система оценки".
quoted_spans pairs each " with the next one, so the spans are '"...оценкой, "' and '" или ... оценки"'; the words на глаз sit
between them, unprotected. relay queue edit with field = "why", old = "на глаз", new = "по ощущению" is accepted and lands:
the owner's verbatim words are changed. Expected: refused, "the edit changes quoted text in why".
The same shape holds in the live items queue-items-store-state-instead-of-dated-events (why: ... исходя из "реального"
состояния объекта") and relay-as-a-portable-tool-project-data-out-of-rel (why: ... каким может стать "вкус", ...).
fix_hint: Pair double quotes by position with nesting: a " after a line start, space, "(", ":" or another opening mark and before a
non-space opens (depth + 1); a " before a line end, space or punctuation closes (depth - 1); a span runs from an opener at
depth 0 to the closer that brings depth back to 0. A mark that fits neither, or a field that ends at depth > 0, makes the
field unbalanced (refused whole). Add the 4 live lines as fixtures in tests/test_queue_edit.py.
pass_cases: 1. why = the live line above (owner quote with an inner "на глаз"): edit old = "на глаз" -> refused, field unchanged, no note.
2. Same line: edit old = "реального" in the queue-items-store-state line, and old = "вкус" in the relay-as-a-portable-tool line -> refused.

3. why = ['all others green, including the new check; "recall-decision never ran" said the log']: edit of the text outside the quote -> accepted (test_replaces_the_fragment_and_adds_a_dated_why_note keeps passing).
4. ['a "b c" d «e» f “g”'] -> spans unchanged: ['"b c"', '«e»', '“g”'] (test_double_guillemet_and_curly_spans).
5. Over the live queue: every one of the 4 lines with Russian outside today's spans is either covered by a span or the edit is refused (the design's section 5 test, which the change does not have).
reason: tests/test_queue_edit.py Quoted::test_nested_double_quotes_are_one_span, test_live_nested_lines_are_covered, EditCommand::test_nested_quoted_word_is_never_changed: pass, fail on base.
findings.summary: a word the owner quoted inside his own quote (nested double quotes) lies outside every protected span, so edit rewrites the owner's words

details: CONFIRMED by probe: "TEST stored: 'tests/t.py::test_new_case'" and "TESTNAME refused: nothing edited: --test is <test file>::...".
The design and brief: "`test` editable only on a closed item, to a test that exists". The test rule runs before _edited_value
computes the result and is given `new`. failing_kind has the same order, but serialize catches its invalid result. Size: 10.
evidence: TESTNAME refused: nothing edited: --test is <test file>::<test name>, or evals/plugin/<case>::<grader> ...
failing_case: Closed item with test = "tests/t.py::test_old_case"; tests/t.py at the default tip defines only test_new.
edit field = "test", old = "tests/t.py::test_old", new = "tests/t.py::test_new": test_refusal checks "tests/t.py::test_new"
(exists), accepts, and stores "tests/t.py::test_new_case", which does not exist. Expected: refused, nothing written.
And the reverse: test = "tests/t.py::test_old", old = "test_old", new = "test_new" is refused with the TEST_FORMS message,
though the result "tests/t.py::test_new" exists. Expected: accepted.
fix_hint: Compute `after = _edited_value(...)` first and pass `after` (the whole new test) to test_refusal; likewise check failing_kind
pass_cases: 1. test "tests/t.py::test_old_case", old "tests/t.py::test_old", new "tests/t.py::test_new" (only test_new defined) -> refused, test unchanged, no note.
2. test "tests/t.py::test_old", old "test_old", new "test_new" (test_new defined) -> accepted, test = "tests/t.py::test_new", one fact note.
3. test "tests/t.py::test_old", old = the whole value, new "tests/t.py::test_missing" -> refused "does not hold a test named test_missing" (today's test keeps passing).
4. Open item -> refused "only after it is closed" (today's test keeps passing).
reason: tests/test_queue_edit.py EditCommand::test_the_test_edit_checks_the_whole_result_not_the_fragment and test_a_test_name_fragment_giving_an_existing_test_is_accepted: pass, fail on base.
findings.summary: edit of `test` checks the `new` fragment, not the test the item ends up naming, so a test that does not exist is stored

details: CONFIRMED by probe (Fence setUp, temp repo): "DELETE passed the fence", "ADD passed the fence". changed_files is built with
--diff-filter=AM, so a deleted file never reaches step_hand_edits; an added one gives before = None and `continue`. The brief:
"nothing but relay's commands writes queue files, on a task branch too"; a lost item is lost data the queue rule exists to
prevent. Size: 15.
failing_case: On a task branch (taken default tip), `git rm .relay/queue/job-item.json && git commit` (git verbs are free in the guard), then
merge: step_queue passes, the item vanishes from the default branch. Expected: refused, naming relay queue drop / relay queue.
Likewise a branch that writes a new .relay/queue/new-one.json by hand (Python, or git show > after the guard): passes.
Expected: refused, naming relay queue add (add lands on the default branch, so an item file only the branch has is hand-made).
fix_hint: In step_hand_edits, diff the range with --diff-filter=AMD (or compare the item lists of the default tip and the branch tip)
and refuse a missing or a new item file unless a migrate module is in the range.
pass_cases: 1. Branch deletes an item file that the default tip has -> step_queue raises Refused naming relay queue.
2. Branch adds an item file the default tip lacks -> Refused naming relay queue add.
3. Branch with a migrate module lib/relay_*migrate*.py that deletes or adds item files -> passes.
4. Branch that took the default branch after a relay queue add landed there -> passes (test_a_library_edit_taken_into_the_branch_passes keeps passing).
5. Branch that closes its item with relay queue done -> passes.
reason: tests/test_queue_edit.py Fence::test_deleting_an_item_file_is_refused, test_adding_an_item_file_by_hand_is_refused, test_a_migrate_module_exempts_added_and_deleted_files: pass, first two fail on base. step_hand_files in merge.py:205.
findings.summary: the hand-edit fence lets a branch delete an item file or add one by hand: deletion is filtered out and a new file is skipped

details: CONFIRMED by reading: grep of the front skill finds `said` only for notes on existing items (line 87); the add sections
(lines 84, 166, 244) are unchanged. The design (section 4 A): "the front skill says the owner's words go there and not into why
or what". The owner chose 2a (new items only) on the premise that new items keep words apart; that depends on the writer
being told. Skill texts get the batched paid run after the wave. Size: 10.
evidence: git diff master...HEAD --stat: no file under plugins/front/skills changed
failing_case: The front adds an item for an out-of-scope question (skill section "An out-of-scope question", line 244): the skill says
relay queue add --input with kind = "feature", nothing about `said`. The front keeps writing "Owner, 27 Oct, verbatim: ..."
into `why` (as this very brief and item do), where relay queue edit can reach the unquoted or nested words (F1).
Expected: the skill's add instructions say the owner's words go to the `said` key of the add input, never into why or what.
fix_hint: One sentence in the front skill where it names relay queue add (and in the delegate skill's add row if it can carry owner words).
pass_cases: 1. plugins/front/skills/front/SKILL.md, where it tells the front to run relay queue add, has a line: the owner's words verbatim go to `said` in the add input, never into why or what.
2. The same line names it for relay queue add --from (or says it does not apply there).
3. rules/queue.md keeps its line on `said` (already present).
reason: plugins/front/skills/front/SKILL.md:246 says the owner's words go to the said key, add --from takes none.
findings.summary: the front skill was not told to put the owner's words in `said`: the owner's answer 2a holds only in rules/queue.md

details: CONFIRMED by reading show_text (unchanged by the diff) and edit (Note("fact", when, ["Edited <field>: ..."])). Readers see the
note, so nothing is wrong today; principle 4 (a field a script reads is structure, not prose) makes the note shape fragile.
Size: 20.
evidence: git diff master...HEAD -- lib/relay_queue.py: show_text and notes_text untouched; edit inserts Note("fact", ..., [f"Edited {field}: {line}" ...])
failing_case: After relay queue edit of why, relay queue show prints "Why:" with the new text and the note "Edited why: ..." among the
notes. The design (section 4 A) promised "Why (edited 27 Oct: ...)" on the field and a note {at, edited: <field>, fact: [...]};
a script can find the edited field only by parsing the note's prose.
fix_hint: Add an `edited` key to the note shape (a migrate-free addition if the parser accepts it), print it in show_text beside the field.
pass_cases: 1. After an edit of why on 10 Oct, show_text prints the Why heading with "(edited 2026-10-10 ...)" or equivalent.
2. The stored note carries the field as data (`edited = "why"`), and notes_text prints it.
3. An item never edited prints "Why:" as today.
findings.summary: show does not mark an edited field, and the edit note is a plain fact 'Edited why: ...' instead of a structured `edited` field
